_comment: Relay's catalogue of voice runtimes and voices. Compiled into the binary
by src/tts/manifest.rs — the UI never constructs a download URL.
The sha256 and size_bytes fields are PROVISIONED AT RELEASE TIME by
scripts/build-voice-manifest.mjs, which downloads each artifact and hashes
it. They are empty here because a checksum cannot be written by hand: an
invented one makes every install fail verification, and a copied one that
nobody checked is worse than none.
While they are empty, VoiceManifest::validate() rejects this file and the
installer reports that automatic setup is unavailable in this build. That
is deliberate: Relay refuses to download an artifact it cannot verify.
To provision:  node scripts/build-voice-manifest.mjs
Each runtime names the exact upstream release it comes from — repo, tag
and asset filename. The generator resolves that asset by name and nothing
else, and validate() re-derives the download URL from those three fields,
so an artifact cannot be swapped for a different one without the change
being visible in this file.
WHY rhasspy/piper AND NOT OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl: the successor project
publishes Python wheels (piper_tts-*.whl) and an sdist, and nothing else —
its release workflow uploads dist/* only. A wheel is a Python package, not
a program: it needs a CPython 3.9+ interpreter and onnxruntime to run.
Relay installs a standalone executable and spawns it, so the last upstream
release that publishes one is what it pins. See docs/talkback/RESEARCH.md.
URLs below are the upstream projects' own release/distribution URLs and are
verified by the generator, which fails if one does not resolve.

voices.description: For Hindi and mixed English-Hindi speech.
